1.title: Governance and Compliance
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Governance and Compliance. It covers the exam area Describe Azure management and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview in Azure. Describe the purpose of Azure Policy. Describe the purpose of resource locks. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure management and governance (thirty to thirty-five percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The governance tools at a glance
1.text: The governance tools at a glance. Microsoft Purview. Purpose in one line: Govern, protect and manage your data across the organization and find compliance risks. Answers the question: "Where is our data, how sensitive is it, and are we compliant?". Azure Policy. Purpose in one line: Enforce rules on resources so they stay compliant. Answers the question: "Are our resources configured the way we require?".

1.title: The governance tools at a glance, continued
1.text: The governance tools at a glance. Resource locks. Purpose in one line: Prevent accidental deletion or change of a resource. Answers the question: "How do we stop someone deleting this by mistake?". Exam tip: Policy equals what is allowed in the configuration. R B A C (Module nine) equals who is allowed to act. Locks equals protect from delete or change, even for an Owner.

1.title: The governance tools at a glance, continued
1.text: The governance tools at a glance. The figure shows this: Purview, Azure Policy and resource locks: what each one governs.

1.title: Microsoft Purview
1.text: Microsoft Purview. Microsoft Purview is a family of data governance, risk and compliance solutions. It gives one view of data across on-premises, multicloud and software-as-a-service sources. Data discovery and catalog. Scans and maps data sources, builds an inventory (data map) and a searchable catalog with classifications. Data classification and labeling. Finds sensitive data (for example credit card numbers) and applies sensitivity labels. Data protection. Helps prevent data loss and control sharing.

1.title: Microsoft Purview, continued
1.text: Microsoft Purview. Compliance management. Helps measure and manage compliance against regulations and standards (for example with a compliance score). Data lineage. Shows where data comes from and how it moves. Use Purview when a question is about knowing, classifying and governing data and compliance risk, not about configuring Azure resources. Exam tip: "Discover and classify sensitive data across the whole organization" to Purview. "Enforce that V Ms can only be created in approved regions" to Azure Policy.

1.title: Azure Policy
1.text: Azure Policy. Azure Policy helps you enforce organizational standards and assess compliance at scale. It evaluates your resources against rules and shows which ones are compliant or non-compliant. Examples of policy rules. Only allow resources in approved regions. Only allow certain V M sizes. Require a tag (such as Cost Center) on every resource. Require encryption or specific settings.

1.title: Azure Policy, continued
1.text: Azure Policy. Policy definition. The rule and the effect (what happens when the rule is not met). Initiative. A group of policy definitions managed together toward one goal (for example a compliance standard). Assignment. Applying a definition or initiative to a scope (management group, subscription, resource group). Effects. Deny (block the action), Audit (flag it), Modify or Append (change or add a property such as a tag), Deploy If Not Exists (create a missing resource). Remediation. Fix existing non-compliant resources. Assignments are inherited down the hierarchy (Module five). Policy evaluates resource properties. It does not give or remove user permissions; that is R B A C.

1.title: Azure Policy, continued
1.text: Azure Policy. A policy can block a non-compliant request even from an Owner. Exam tip: Deny blocks creation; audit only reports. Initiative equals bundle of policies. A policy assigned at a management group applies to all subscriptions below.

1.title: Resource locks
1.text: Resource locks. A resource lock prevents accidental deletion or modification of an Azure resource, resource group or subscription. Delete (Can Not Delete). What it blocks: Deleting. Allowed: Reading and modifying. Read-only. What it blocks: Deleting and modifying. Allowed: Reading only.

1.title: Resource locks, continued
1.text: Resource locks. Key facts. Locks apply to all users and roles, even Owners. To change or delete a locked resource you must remove the lock first (which needs permission to manage locks). Locks are inherited: a lock on a resource group applies to every resource in it, including ones added later. A read-only lock can cause surprising effects (for example you may be unable to start a stopped V M or list keys). Locks protect against management-plane actions, not data changes inside a service (for example writing a blob). Exam tip: "Protect a production resource group from being deleted by mistake" to delete lock on the resource group. "Even the subscription Owner cannot delete it" to lock.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors must ensure that every resource is created only in the East U S and West Europe regions. Which service enforces this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Policy. Azure Policy evaluates and can deny resources that break a rule such as allowed locations.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A production resource group must be protected from accidental deletion, even by an Owner. What should be applied? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A delete lock on the resource group. A delete lock blocks deletion for all users until the lock is removed. Tags have no protective effect.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants to find and classify sensitive data such as card numbers across on-premises and cloud sources. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Microsoft Purview. Purview discovers, classifies and governs data and helps manage compliance risk.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What is an initiative in Azure Policy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A group of policy definitions managed together. An initiative bundles related policy definitions toward one goal.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A policy has the Audit effect and a V M is created that breaks the rule. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The V M is created and flagged as non-compliant. Audit reports non-compliance without blocking. Deny would block.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which lock type allows a resource to be changed but not deleted? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Delete (Can Not Delete). A delete lock prevents deletion; modification is still allowed. A read-only lock blocks both.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of Azure Policy? Answer: Enforce organizational standards and assess resource compliance. Question two. What does Microsoft Purview do? Answer: Governs and protects data across the organization and helps manage compliance. Question three. Name the two lock types. Answer: Delete (Can Not Delete) and Read-only.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Do locks apply to Owners? Answer: Yes. The lock must be removed first. Question five. What is a policy initiative? Answer: A group of policy definitions assigned together. Question six. Policy or R B A C: which controls who may act? Answer: R B A C. Policy controls what resource configurations are allowed.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Purview: data governance and compliance: discover, classify, label, lineage, across on-premises, multicloud and sass. Azure Policy: rules for resources: deny, audit, modify, deploy If Not Exists; initiatives bundle policies; inherited. Locks: delete lock or read-only lock; even Owners blocked; inherited; remove the lock first. Policy versus R B A C: policy equals allowed configuration; R B A C equals allowed people and actions. In the next module, we continue the course.
